name: Bedja
title: Levite in Temple Service
summary: Bedja was a Levite mentioned in connection with the time of Ezra and Nehemiah. He was among those who returned to Jerusalem after the exile in Babylon and participated in rebuilding the spiritual life in Israel. His name appears in lists of Levites who served in the temple and took part in the renewal of the covenant.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among the Levites
keyEvents.description: Bedja is mentioned among the Levites who served in connection with the return from exile and the rebuilding of temple service in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Participation in the Renewal of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: The Levites, including Bedja, took part in the great renewal of the covenant under Nehemiah's leadership, where the people committed themselves to follow God's law.

keyEvents.title: Commitment to Separate from Foreign Wives
keyEvents.description: Bedja was among those who committed to sending away their foreign wives in line with Ezra's reforms to preserve the purity of the people.

keyEvents.title: The Role of the Levites in Teaching the Law
keyEvents.description: The Levites, to which Bedja belonged, helped the people understand the law when Ezra read it aloud to the assembly.
